title: Design System: 欸哩照顧手冊 · Grouped Care Notes

large-title.purpose: The dog's name, once, beside the avatar.

section-title.purpose: Section headings in the section's colour; the emergency first row at 800.

closing.purpose: The thank-you line at the end of the page.

row-key.purpose: First line of every row (500 in key-value rows).

detail.purpose: Second line of a row and key-value values; in ink when it is the instruction itself.

group-header.purpose: In-section group labels in secondary ink.

caption.purpose: Tab labels at 15px (800 on the current tab); the smallest size.

shadows.name: frosted-bar
shadows.purpose: Translucent bottom tab bar over content; the only depth effect. No box-shadows on the page.

motion.name: none
motion.purpose: The page is still; tab taps use the browser default anchor jump, no smooth scroll.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.purpose: Single centred column max width; the tab bar items share it. No other breakpoints.

narrative.overview:
The handbook is the category standard played straight: it should read like notes and reminders the phone itself ships, at the craft level of Apple Reminders and Apple Health, without their branding. It is read, not operated: there is no checklist, no stored state and nothing to tick. A cool grey grouped ground carries white rounded sections; rows are a bold key over a quieter detail line, separated by inset hairlines; titles are large and bold. The readers are elderly parents opening a LINE link on a phone, so everything is set larger than the platform default (19px body, 20px row keys, 34px title) and nothing important is faint.

The page opens on the title and goes straight into the owner's four requests; there is no summary or status card. Each section is announced the Health way: a coloured line glyph beside a section title in the same colour (the four requests and the daily routine in caramel, food amber, walks green, habits blue, emergency red, the dog's profile a grey glyph under an ink title). Colour identifies a section's glyph and title and nothing else; rows stay white with ink text. Red belongs to 不舒服時 alone. Dark mode is the platform's true-black grouped scheme, not a tinted variant.

The single illustration is a small drawn avatar of the dog in a 64px circle beside the title, made of flat filled planes and following the owner's photo (chocolate tricolour long coat, white blaze and muzzle, tan brows and cheeks, yellow harness). The photo itself is not published. The page is still: apart from the browser's default anchor jump, nothing moves.
keyCharacteristics: Grouped-inset system UI: grey ground, white 14px-radius sections, hairlines inset 16px from the leading edge.
Notes, not tasks: key-over-detail rows, written-out rules, no checkboxes, counts, status cards or stored state.
One warm caramel accent for the two leading sections, the current tab (tinted pill + 800 weight), inline times and focus.
Section identity by coloured glyph + coloured title only (Health manner), never colour-square tiles.
System sans at enlarged sizes; secondary text is a dark grey that keeps ≥7.8:1.
A fixed translucent bottom tab bar with five destinations; emergency always reachable in one tap.

rules.name: The One Warm Accent Rule
rules.body: Caramel is the only accent. It marks what leads (the four requests, the routine), where you are (the current tab's pill) and focus; no second accent is introduced.

rules.name: The Red Is Unwell Rule
rules.body: Red appears only in the 不舒服時 section and its tab. It never marks a meal, a request or a forbidden food (the 不能給他吃 bullets are grey).

rules.name: The Title-Not-Tile Rule
rules.body: A section's colour lives in its line glyph and its title text. Never put the glyph on a filled colour square; that reads as Settings, which the owner rejected.

rules.name: The Nothing Small Rule
rules.body: No text below 15px, row content at 18px or larger, and no faint tint for content a parent must read; secondary text is a dark grey, never a lowered opacity.

rules.name: The Phrase Break Rule
rules.body: Chinese lines break between phrases: running text is wrapped in inline-block phrase spans (`.seg`) so a line never splits mid-phrase.

rules.name: The Bold Lead-In Rule
rules.body: When one row carries alternative rules, each rule is its own detail line in ink, opened by a bold condition word and a full-width space (**有吃完**　… / **沒吃**　…). The cases are written out; the reader never has to answer a control to see them.

rules.name: The Flat Sections Rule
rules.body: Sections never float. Depth is the grey/white step; nothing on the page casts a shadow.

dos: **Do** put every new block of content in a white 14px-radius section on the grouped ground, with inset hairline separators between rows.
**Do** announce a new section with a line glyph from the sprite (24-unit grid, 2px round stroke) and a title in the same colour.
**Do** write alternative rules out in full as ink detail lines with a bold lead-in, rather than hiding one behind a control.
**Do** use the accent for what leads, where you are and focus, and accent-ink whenever caramel sets text; mark the current place with fill and weight as well as colour.
**Do** keep body text at 19px, details at 18px and nothing below 15px; secondary text in ink-2, never by opacity.
**Do** wrap Chinese phrases in `.seg` spans so lines break between phrases.
**Do** define every new colour in both the light and the true-black dark set, and keep text pairs at 4.5:1 or better.
donts: **Don't** place a section glyph on a filled colour square or build Settings-style rows (the owner rejected anything settings-like).
**Don't** use red outside 不舒服時 and its tab.
**Don't** add checkboxes, progress counts, a summary or status card, or saved state; the owner asked for notes and reminders only.
**Don't** add decorated pet-app cuteness (stickers, paw-print patterns, cartoon type) or dashboard stat cards; the owner named childish, sticker-like, busy and cold-app-like as wrong.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients or motion; the page is still.
**Don't** publish the owner's photo of the dog; the drawn avatar stands in for it.
